chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Opening in Chicago with a very loud band
summary: Billed like a circus after leaving Goodman, Cootie's loud band opened in Chicago in a high-class nightclub where it was too much.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: We still have a little time to discuss the success of Cootie Williams at the Savoy.
Yeah. You said he went in there.
Yeah, he went in there. Let me see... We didn't open up there. We opened up in Chicago.
These recordings in '42 were made in Chicago, April 1.

The band opened in Chicago, I think. I'm trying to think how often we'd get to Chicago. I'm not sure. Where did we open at? I don't know. Greely could tell you that. But I remember when we did open in Chicago, he was billed like a circus around Chicago. You know, he had just come out of Benny Goodman's band, and he was billed like a circus. And...
I said that people were expecting that. But Cootie comes down with the baton, and we played the loudest number

Cootie had in the book. And at that place, you did not have to blow loud to be heard. And Cootie had a big band. I don't know how many pieces were in the band. A full band. And we hit down there like a ton of bricks. Boy, people were holding their ears, and he was playing his favorite number, "Rollin'" And boy, it was loud. I don't know if the people liked it or not. It was really too loud, you know.

Well, anyway, the type of music that Cootie was playing, it wasn't for no high-class people. I mean, he was playing the rugcutters music. You know what you could do to the Lindy... I say it was Lindy Hop; of course, it wasn't the Lindy Hop then. But you could do the Lindy Hop (?). One of them things. He had a dance band, a dance-hall band. And boy, we was wailin'! And this is in a high-class nightclub, which...it really didn't fit in the place. But anyway, I forget how many months we stayed there. We were there practically all winter. It's cold in Chicago, too.
